title: First settlers
description: Voyagers from Sri Lanka and South India settle the atolls, whose people will be Buddhist for most of the next sixteen centuries.

title: Maldives converts to Islam
description: The last Buddhist king becomes Sultan Muhammad al-Adil, and the Maldives has been a Muslim sultanate most of the time since.

title: Ibn Battuta visits
description: The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta stays over a year, is made chief judge and leaves a classic account of the island sultanate.

title: Thakurufaanu retakes Malé
description: Muhammad Thakurufaanu drives out the Portuguese garrison that had held Malé for fifteen years and becomes sultan, restoring Maldivian independence.

title: Pyrard shipwrecked
description: The French traveller François Pyrard is wrecked on the reefs and spends five years in the islands, later publishing the fullest early European account of them.

title: British protectorate
description: The sultan puts the islands' foreign relations in British hands; Britain protects the Maldives through Ceylon without stationing officials there.

title: First constitution
description: The sultan grants the Maldives' first written constitution and an elected majlis, after unrest in the over-taxed islands.

title: First republic
description: A vote abolishes the sultanate and makes Mohamed Amin Didi president, but the republic collapses in riots within eight months and the sultanate returns.

title: Independence
description: Britain ends its protection after 78 years and the Maldives becomes fully independent, keeping the sultanate for now.

title: Second republic
description: A referendum engineered by prime minister Ibrahim Nasir abolishes the sultanate and proclaims a republic, which has endured since.

title: First tourist resort
description: Kurumba opens as the first island resort, the start of the tourism that now dominates the Maldivian economy.

title: British leave Gan
description: The Royal Air Force pulls out of its staging post on Gan after London declines to pay a higher rent, closing the last direct British presence.

title: Gayoom becomes president
description: Maumoon Abdul Gayoom succeeds Nasir and rules for thirty years, winning six referendums with no opposition allowed.

title: Coup attempt defeated by India
description: Maldivian plotters and Sri Lankan Tamil mercenaries seize parts of Malé, and Indian paratroopers fly in overnight in Operation Cactus and save the government.

title: First multiparty election
description: Former political prisoner Mohamed Nasheed defeats Gayoom in a run-off, ending thirty years of one-man rule.

title: Underwater cabinet meeting
description: President Nasheed chairs a cabinet meeting in scuba gear on the seabed to dramatise the threat of rising seas to the lowest country on Earth.

title: Nasheed resigns
description: After a police mutiny over the arrest of a judge, Nasheed resigns in what he calls a coup at gunpoint.

title: Yameen elected president
description: Abdulla Yameen, Gayoom's half-brother, wins after two annulled rounds and rules with an authoritarian hand.

title: Solih elected president
description: Opposition candidate Ibrahim Mohamed Solih unexpectedly defeats Yameen and restores competitive politics.
